120 THIRTY-SECOND REPORT V. S. CIVIL SERVICE COMMISSION. December 1, 1914. Mrs. Onie Cummings maybe appointed as a clerk in the Department of Agriculture without reference to the civil-service rules at a salary of $900 per annum. This order is issued upon the recommendation of the Secretary of Agriculture, who states that Mrs. Cummings 's training and experience are such as to enable her to render good service. She is the widow of Mr. R. F. Cummings, formerly a clerk at a salary of $1,400 per annum in the Bureau of Soils, Department of Agriculture. Mr. Cummings was in the service from October 16, 1906, until February 1, 1914, the date of his death. The Civil Service Commission does not concur in the recommendation of the Secre- tary of Agriculture. December 7, 1914. Miss Louisa W. Happersett may be appointed to a position in the classified civil service without reference to the civil-service rules. This order is issued upon the recommendation of the Secretary of War, who states that the Quartermaster General, the Surgeon General, and the Judge Advocate General of the Army unite in requesting the issuance of an Executive order. Miss Happersett is the daughter of the late John C. G. Happersett, major and surgeon, Umted States Army, who rendered highly efl&cient military service during a period of 32 years, including the 4 years of the Civil War. The Surgeon General and the Judge Advocate General call special attention to the services rendered by Maj. Happersett and his family during the yellow-fever epidemic at Fort Brown, Tex., in 1882. The Civil Service Commission does not concur in recommending the order. December 11, 1914. Mrs. Sallie G. Jones, who has been employed in the Indian Bureau of the Interior Department for a period of four years, may be promoted without examination under the civil-service rules. Mrs. Jones has been employed in the Interior Department in various capacities since May, 1900. Her record for efficient and faithful service is good. She was placed in the classified service imder an Executive order issued October 9, 1908, and appointed copyist at $720 per annum. In October, 1910, she was promoted to $900, and in April, 1914, in view of the meritorious service which she was rendering, the Commissioner of Indian Affairs promoted her to a clerical position at $1,000 per annum. However, owing to a ruling of the Civil Service Commission that under the provisions of the Executive order placing her in the classified service, she was not eligible for promotion to said grade without examination, she was, on August 16, 1914, reduced to $900 per annum. Mis. Jones is the widow of Robert Tyler Jones, a g^randson of President Tyler, who was bom in the White House diuing the administration of President Tyler, and who, it is stated, was the only male child ever bom in the White House. December 19, 1914. Mrs. John L. Evans may be appointed to the position of charwoman under the superintendent of the State, War, and Navy Departments building without regard to the labor relations governing appointments of laborers in Washington. Mrs. Evans is the wiaow of John L. Evans, who was discharged a corporal from Company H, Twenty-second United States Infantry, July 12, 1902, character excel- lent. From July, 1902, until January 24, 1914, he was employed in the navy yard in this city. On said date, while working as a machinist's helper at the navy ^ard, a hammer flew off the handle and stmck him on the head, from the effects of which he died June 18, 1914, after a long illness and much suffering, leaving a wife and two small children. The acting superintendent of the State, War, and Navy Departments building recommends that an Executive order be issued authorizing the appointment of Mrs. Evans. The Civil Service Commission does not concur in the recommendation. - (It will be noted that this order waives the labor regulations, and not the civil- service rules.) December 30, 1914. Mr. Calvin Satterfield, of Pennsylvania, maybe appointed to the position of Chief of the Division of Accounts, Department of Justice, without reference to the civil- service rules. Digitized by Google
EXECUTIVE OEDEBS. 121 This order is issued upon the recommendation of the Attorney General, who states that the position of Chief of the Division of Accounts is highly confidential, and requires a peculiar order of talent; that a diligent effort has been made within the classified service to find some one possessing the required qualifications, but without success. The Attorney General believes that Mr. Satterfield, who is known to him personally, is especially qualified for the position, and that the interests of the public would be subserved by exempting the appointment. The Civil Service Commission does not concur in the recommendation. January 5, 1015. Fred W. Carrington may be promoted from assistant messenger in the Pension Bureau to the clenc»l grade without examination under the civil-service rules. This order is issued upon the recommendation of the Secretary of the Interior, in rec(^nition of an ingenious and public-spirited employee who has built and put into operation a mechanical device and allowed the Government to take out patents for it. January 7, 1015. Mrs. Inez M. Clark and Miss Emily I. Kramer may be appointed clerks in the Bureau of War Risk Insurance in the Treasury Department without reference to the civil -service rules. This order is issued upon the recommendation of the Secretary of the Treasury, who states that on account of the technical character of the work required specially trained clerks are needed, and that Mrs. Clark and Miss Kramer have demonstrated that they possess the peculiar Qualifications necessary. The Civil Service Commission does not concur in the recommendation. January 7, 1015. It is hereby ordered that the physical requirements be waived in order that Mr. George P. Kinsman, of the battleship Vermont^ who lost his right leg as the result of injuries sustained during the occupation of Vera Cruz by the American troops in April, 1914, may take the clerk-earner examination in the postal service. January 0, 1015. Mr. Charles A. Ljrerly, jr., is herebv permitted to take the examination in accordance with law for appointment as second, lieutenant in the Engineer Corps of the Army. He has passed the civil-service examination for junior engineer, but his eligibility has expired. This order is issued upon the recommendation of the Secretary of War and the Chief of Engineers, with the concurrence of the Civil Service Commission. January 20, 1015. Mr. Newton C. Llewellyn maybe reinstated as a carrier in the Knoxville, Tenn., post office without regard to the length of his separation from the service. Mr. Llewellyn entered the Postal Service as a substitute carrier at Knoxville on January 18, 1895, and remained in the service until February 28, 1907, when he resigned. The Postmaster General states that Mr. Llewellyn's record is good, that it is a meritorious case, and that the department has no objection to the issuance of an order. The Civil Service Commission does not recommend this order. January 21, 1015. The year limit upon eligibility for reinstatement is extended to pennit the rein- statement of Harold J. Wagner to a clerkship in the Department of Justice. Mr. Wagner was appointed through examination on June 26, 1905, as a clerk in the service of the Panama Canal, and served until June 9, 1906. On September 4, 1906, he was appointed to a clerkship in the Department of Justice, and served until April 9, 1909, when he resigned from the position of telegrapher and stenographer at $1,200 to accept a position on the Newfoundland Fisheries Arbitration Commission under the State Department. He continued in this position until September, 1910, when he was appointed secretary of the Chamizal Aroitration Conmiission under the State Department, in which position he served until the completion of the work in August, 1911. His duties in these positions are said to have been principally legal. He did not seek retransfer to the classified service because he was compelled to undergo an operation which incapacitated him for 15 months. From February 1 to June 30, 1914, he served as record clerk with the American-British Claims Arbitration Com- Digitized by Google
